title: Why a Cold Glass Gets Wet

visual.title: A cold glass, a surprising puddle
visual.statement: The water comes from the air.

narration.text: A cold glass can get wet on the outside, even when nothing spills. The glass is not leaking water. Where does that water come from?
The air contains water vapor. When air next to the glass cools enough, some of that vapor condenses into liquid droplets.

visual.title: Condensation, not a leak
visual.statement: Tiny droplets can join and run down.

narration.text: Those droplets join together and run down the outside. The puddle came from moisture in the surrounding air. This familiar process is called condensation.
